Commentary.Commentary: So, that's it from us! Afghanistan cricket takes another step forward, a big step forward, with this emphatic whitewash over Bangladesh. The Tigers will be disappointed with their outing in this series, especially how they fared with the bat. Plenty to work on for them. Anyway, we thank you for your company and hope you join us for future matches. In the meantime, you can switch tabs and catch all the action from the 1st Test between West Indies and Sri Lanka. Cheers!

Asghar Stanikzai says he's happy they won the series 3-0. Reckons this series has been a good preparation for the upcoming Test series against India. Feels all the players have been working very hard to improve Afghanistan cricket on the whole. Adds that everyone is doing their job in all the departments and as a result, everything falls in place. Thanks his board for the continued support and also the crowd for its support throughout the series.

Shakib Al Hasan says his side performed better than the first two games so is disappointed they lost out tonight. Feels they restricted Afghanistan to a reasonable total and rues the middle overs where they didn't score as many as they would have liked. Applauds Rahim and Mahmudullah for their effort and says anything can happen in a T20 game as everything is so close. Admits there are plenty of areas they can work on and will get down to it as soon as possible.

Man of the Series, Rashid Khan, thanks the Almighty first up. Is happy as they won the game and is delighted he's able to execute his skills and perform for his side. Emphasizes that it's important to enjoy every ball and that's what helps him do so well. Mentions that with the way the wicket was, it was important to bowl in the good length areas. Credits his fitness mainly for his success as he stresses that it's important in every department of the game. Ends by thanking the crowd for its continued support throughout the series and hopes he and his side can come back soon to play again in Dehradun.

Man of the Match, Mushfiqur Rahim, says he knew it was going to be a difficult task. Thought they were a few runs short in the last over because it's quite hard to score so many runs. Credits Afghanistan for the way they played and vows to come back stronger whenever they play Afghanistan next. Reckons 145 was a par score and with the bowlers the Afghans have, it's a difficult task as it is. States that they lost a few early wickets but knew that he and Mahmudullah could do it if they took the game deep, but Rashid Khan bowled a superb last over which they couldn't overcome.

The Afghans were terrific for the most part with the ball and in the field as well. They applied a lot of pressure on the Bangladeshi batsmen. Had someone from the top order managed to do just a bit more, the outcome could have probably ended differently. Earlier in the evening, a solid start from the Afghan openers and some late hitting from the middle order saw them get to a total which eventually proved to be just enough.

With 9 needed off the final over, Rashid Khan proved once again why he's held in such high regard. He dismissed Rahim off the first ball and kept things really tight. But, on this night, even he needed some assistance and it came via some outstanding work in the field from Shafiq. If not for his heroics right at the end, Bangladesh would have won this game. A superb effort all around.

A cliffhanger of a contest has come to a close. It went right down to the wire but Afghanistan clinched the victory to whitewash Bangladesh 3-0 to take the series by storm. With a target of 146 in front of them, the Tigers did not get off to the best of starts. Were 35/3 inside the Powerplay and looking down and out. But, Rahim and Mahmudullah stepped up to the plate and took it on their shoulders to put up a fight. That 19th over gave them a real impetus where Rahim scored 21 runs against Janat.

AFGHANISTAN WIN BY 1 RUN! But what drama on the final delivery. Oh, dear me! Dear me! Shafiqullah Shafiq, you absolute beauty. Talk about a stunning effort to win your side the match. Unbelievable stuff. Fuller in length around off, Haque lofts it down towards long on. Shafiq is the man there, he moves to his left and leaps to get his hands to the ball. He still has a lot of work to do as the ball starts to travel across the rope. He moves swiftly once again, stretches low and pulls it back in. Nabi from long off comes to the ball and throws it back in towards Shahzad. He collects the ball and whips the bails off as the batsmen are coming back for the third. Mahmudullah is the batsman who's out and Afghanistan celebrate. But, they are going to have to wait a moment as the umpire wants to check if it's a boundary or not. It's taken upstairs and the replays show that Shafiq managed to do just enough to keep the ball in. Phew!

Is that a boundary? Have Bangladesh won? Have Afghanistan pulled it off? Shafiqullah Shafiq the man in the limelight and it's over to the TV umpire to determine whether he's made a clean save or not. So close. Let's see what happens here...
Quite full and quicker in pace, slogged through to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Loopy leg break around off, Haque plays it off the outer edge towards short third man for a run. Mahmudullah on strike now, 5 needed in 2. What's going to happen here?
Runs will be welcome no matter how they come by Bangladesh. Fuller outside off, Haque goes down to sweep and gets it off the under edge through the keeper's legs for a double.
Googly on middle and leg, spinning in, Mahmudullah gets some bat on it as it goes down towards short fine leg. Quick run taken.
Ariful Haque walks into the middle next.

OUT! Rashid Khan strikes off the very first ball! Mushfiqur Rahim holes out. His favourite shot, the momentum on his side and it's an unfortunate dismissal for his side. Tossed up on the stumps, Rahim gets down and slog sweeps. It's flat and right towards Najibullah out at deep mid-wicket, who dives forward and takes a superb catch.
Rashid Khan will bowl the final over. He has 8 to defend. All happening here. Going to a superb one, whichever way it goes.
No! Just the single. But it's still a phenomenal over. 21 from it. Rahim digs out the yorker and keeps strike.

FOUR! What a gem of a knock Rahim is playing here. Batting of the highest quality. Overpitched on off stump, Rahim gets low and brings out the reverse sweep. The placement is perfect as he beats the diving backward point fielder for the fifth boundary of the over. 6 in 6 coming up?
FOUR! 4 boundaries in 4 balls. This is sensational from the veteran Mushfiqur Rahim. He's seeing his side home here. Lofts this full ball over mid off comfortably. 14 needed in 7 now.
FOUR! Three in a row. This time it's too full, Rahim takes full advantage of it by staying leg side. He drills this past mid off and finds the fence.

FOUR! Two in two for Rahim! This is stupendous batting. Shortish in length, Rahim goes across the line this time and pulls it through mid-wicket. Beats the man in the deep and sends it across the rope for a boundary.
FOUR! Good start to the over for Bangladesh. Short and wide, Rahim flays this over point and finds the fence. Needs to push in this over, it's the crucial one.
Karim Janat brought back to bowl.
What an over. Just 3 from the over, superb comeback from Rashid Khan. Slightly quicker through the air on off, Mahmudullah taps it down right under his nose. 30 to win off the final 2 overs.
Quite full and outside off, the batsman looks to hit it across the line but gets beaten.
Shorter outside off, cut through to deep backward point for a run.
Keeps it right up there once more, just outside off. Rahim moves across and then gets low to sweep but can't connect.
Full in length, it goes off the leading edge towards covers. Quick run taken.
Turning away from around off, Rahim with an angled bat steers it through point for one run.
FOUR! Yes, he can! 15 off the over. This is sensational. Full and in the slot for Mahmudullah, he goes deep inside the crease and lofts it over mid off for a one bounce boundary.

Could very well be. Runs comes in a streaky manner on this occasion but it's all the same to the Tigers. Length ball and it takes the inside edge of Mahmudullah's bat. Shahzad dives to his left but it's past him. Two runs taken. The 50-run stand is up. 11 off the over, can he finish with a boundary?

SIX! Another full toss and this time he pays the price for it. Mahmudullah backs away and swings across the line. Clears the mid-wicket boundary and gets a maximum. Is this the over that Bangladesh needed?
Low full toss on middle stump, whipped through mid-wicket. Mahmudullah runs the first one hard and as a result manages to come back for the second.
Short ball down the leg side, Mahmudullah goes for the big pull but misses. No caught behind given, which makes not giving it a wide a bit strange.
Another leg bye. A length ball on the stumps, Rahim swings across the line and misses. It goes off the thigh pad on the off side as the batsmen change ends.

Shout for a leg before. Not given. Height the issue? Maybe pitching outside leg as well. Not sure. Anyway, it's a beauty from Khan. Pitches the leg break around leg and it spins sharpy. Rahim can't connect as the ball goes off his pads towards short third man. A leg bye is taken.
Touch short outside off, steered to the left of backward point for a single.
Quicker through the air, on off, hit right back at the bowler.
Some air provided outside off, Rahim drags the sweep to deep mid-wicket and changes ends.
Turning in from middle and leg, Rahim shuffles across to play the scoop shot this time but fails to connect.

FOUR! Dangerous shot to play but he's executed it well. All about execution. Nicely done. Tossed right up there, Rahim quickly gets low, positions himself for the reverse sweep and places it between short third man and backward point for a boundary.
Rashid Khan is finally brought back into the bowling attack.
Varying the pace again, shorter in length once more, Mahmudullah throws his bat at it and misses. Dot ball to end the over. 55 needed in 30.
Full toss and Rahim drives it towards covers. Sets off and completes the run. There is a shy at the bowler's end but it misses.
Full in length, outside off, driven square through point for an easy one.
Short in length, slower in pace again, Rahim backs away to pull but misses and so does the diving keeper. It goes behind and the batsmen take a run. Bye signalled by the umpire.
Cutting back in from a length, whipped off the pads through to square leg for a run.

Top edge but it lands safely. Slower back of a length delivery in line of the stumps, Rahim swings across the line and gets a top edge which lands just short of the man at fine leg. Single to the total.
Aftab Alam to bowl once more.
Mahmudullah shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Yorker darted in, dug out square on the off side for a brace.

SIX! Much-needed hit for Bangladesh. Need more of these, a lot more. Tossed up around off, Mahmudullah plants his front foot forward and slogs it high and handsome over the mid-wicket fence for half a dozen.
Plays with the spins as he turns it away on the leg side.

Not out! Good effort though once again in the field from an Afghan fielder. Rahim works this towards point and the batsmen take off. Mujeeb collects the ball and hits the stumps at the non-striker's end. The third umpire is called into action and replays show Rahim has just made it in. Single completed.
Direct hit! Is Mushfiqur Rahim in trouble? Mujeeb scores the bull's eye and it's taken upstairs. Looks close...
Turning in on middle and leg, Mahmudullah backs away and punches it off the middle to sweeper cover. One run taken.
Mohammad Nabi is back.
Eases it away through the mid on region and a single is collected.
Clips it away with the spin through the vacant spaces in the mid-wicket area and calls his partner through for a run.
Full and attacking the stumps, quicker in pace, it's played back to the bowler.
Touch shorter in length outside off, Rahim pushes it to the left of the bowler for nothing.
Goes back and whips it through to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Turning in from around off, stays back and punches it to covers.
Mujeeb Ur Rahman is called back.
Banged in short, Rahim leaps and fails to connect with his ramp shot. 73 required to win for Bangladesh off 48 deliveries.
Comes forward with a step and pushes it to long on. Rotates strike with a single.

Make that three in a row. Bangladesh cannot afford these if they want to get close to the target. Length ball on the fifth stump line, the batsman gets a bottom edge behind to the keeper on the bounce.
Consecutive dot ball for Janat. Good stuff. Just behind a length, quite close to off, Mahmudullah misses his attempted cut shot.
Full again, outside off this time, driven firmly but straight to the cover fielder.
FOUR! Full and on the pads, easy enough for Mahmudullah to put this away. Just works it fine down the leg side with his wrists and sends it across the fine leg fence.
Karim Janat back on to bowl.
The batsman tried to sweep that one but missed it and was hit on the pads. Good first over from the leggie.
Googly on a flatter trajectory, it's flicked away through to deep mid-wicket for a run.

FOUR! That's gone away for a boundary but don't be deceived, was closer to getting a wicket. Superb bowling from Rashid. He brings out the leg break and Mahmudullah is in two minds whether to play at it or not. It pops off the higher part of the bat, past the slip fielder and away to the third man boundary.
Opens the face and dabs it away square towards point.
Closer to the off stick, the straighter one, blocked.

Starts off with a googly on middle, turns in which Rahim doesn't pick. It goes off the pad after taking the bat as it goes fine down the leg side. The fielder from short fine leg chases it down and saves a run for his side.
Rashid Khan is brought into the bowling attack.
Comes ahead to this fuller length delivery and offers a defensive shot in response.
Nabi bowls it on a shorter length, the batsman keeps it out off the back foot.
Played to the point region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Tossed up outside off, Mahmudullah comes forward and wrists it through mid on for one more.
Touch straight in line, Rahim nudges it just wide of short fine leg to get off strike.
Touch shorter in length, spinning in from outside off, Mahmudullah goes back and offers a firm punch down to long on for one.
Mohammad Nabi is back on.
Works this away on the leg side and keeps strike with a run. 90 needed in 11 overs.
The batsman plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. They pick up a single.
Back of a length outside off, Mahmudullah punches it off the back foot through the covers and takes a single to get off the mark.
Mahmudullah is the next man in to bat.

OUT! Samiullah Shenwari... Or should I say, Samiullah Rhodes? What a catch! Oh, what a catch! Unreal stuff from one of Afghanistan's best players in this series. And what a time to pull something like this off too. The Bangladesh captain is out of here. Janat bowls a slower one full in length, Shakib jumps out and tries to clear the cover area. Shenwari there moves to his right and dives full stretch as the ball sticks in his right hand. Superb stuff. Afghanistan are in the driving seat here.

Safe! He survives. Shakib taps this length ball to point and takes off. Najibullah gets to the ball quickly and as a result, Shakib has to get back. He plants his bat back in and there's a direct hit at his end. The umpire takes it upstairs and replays show that he's just in.
Another run out appeal. Taken upstairs by the umpire, though this time the batsman looks safe. Shakib is the man in question.

SIX! A little pick-up shot from Shakib Al Hasan and it's travelled the distance. Marvellous cricket shot. Fuller on the stumps, the Bangladesh skipper just lifts it and dumps it over square leg for a maximum.
Charges out to this length ball and slaps it towards mid off. Can't beat the fielder. Just 3 runs off the over.
A mistimed cut shot from Rahim. Gets it off the bottom edge towards point. Dot ball.
Fuller from the bowler, Shakib makes a little room, comes down the track and drives it through the right of the bowler for a run.
Works this with an angled bat and runs it down to third man for one run.

Good with the bat and now superb in the field too. Wonderful effort from Samiullah Shenwari. Shakib thrashes this full delivery on off towards extra cover. Shenwari moves quickly to his left and dives to stop the ball. Had he not stopped that, it was a certain boundary. Just the single for the batsmen.
Length delivery around off, moving away off the seam, it's dabbed away from the body with soft hands on the off side.
Aftab Alam is called back on for a bowl.
Full ball attacking the stumps, Shakib gets his front leg out of the way and drives it towards mid off for a quick single.
Leans ahead to this fullish ball and taps it in front of point. Calls for the run early and manages to complete it with ease. Good running.
Wide! Goes quite full on this occasion, but too far outside off again. It goes from the other side of the tramline and the umpire raises his arms sideways.
Marginally ahead of a length, in the channel outside off, hit hard but straight to the cover fielder.
FOUR! Beautiful shot. Length delivery outside off, some width offered and it's enough for Rahim to cut it right in the gap. Past point and it's away to the boundary line.
Wide! Too far outside off, across the tramline, wide signalled by the umpire.
Works this away just wide of mid on and gets off strike with a single.
Stifled appeal for an lbw, but rightly turned down by the umpire. The ball pitched outside leg. Catches Shakib on the pads but it won't matter.
Karim Janat into the bowling attack now.
Short and wide outside off, Rahim looks to cut it away but misses. Bangladesh are 35/3 at the end of the Powerplay and they need 111 runs to win off 84 balls.
Shakib Al Hasan makes his way out to the middle.

OUT! Another huge mix-up which results in another run out. What is going on out there? Bangladesh are shooting themselves in the foot with these unnecessary things. Rahim works this down to short fine leg and Das takes off this time. Several yes and nos later, Liton is found struggling like his just-dismissed partner. Runs back, but the throw is already in from Alam to Nabi as he takes the bails off. Das is well short.
Rahim goes with the spin as he turns it through mid-wicket and gets off the mark with a double.
Spinning in from around off, Das works it in front of square leg for a run.
Mushfiqur Rahim is the new batsman in.

OUT! He's gone! Huge mix-up in the middle sees Sarkar walk back to the dugout. Das swings it and off the inner half plays it down towards short fine leg. Hesitation on the run and eventually Sarkar has to rush back to his end. But, it's a little too late as Karim Janat throws it back to Nabi who takes the bails off in a flash. The replays are a mere formality here as they confirm even the dive doesn't save Soumya. A timely breakthrough for Afghanistan.
A run out appeal against Soumya Sarkar is referred upstairs. He looks to be gone here.
Waits for the ball to come, opens the face and runs it just wide of short third man for a single.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.

Huge shout for an lbw, not given. Full toss from Mujeeb, right on the boot of Sarkar who can't get any bat on it as he is beaten for pace. The umpire shakes his head as it's going down leg. He'll feel fortunate.

SIX! Unreal shot from the southpaw. Beautiful execution. Full on the stumps, Sarkar positions himself quickly for the reverse sweep and nails it to perfection. Clears the third man fence and earns a biggie to his name.
Arm ball coming in with the angle, on leg, Sarkar misses the flick and wears it on the pads.

FOUR! Edged and just wide! Tossed up outside off, Sarkar plays the expansive drive but gets an edge just past a diving Mohammad Nabi at first slip. He moves to his left but it comes towards him too fast. It goes away to the third man fence for a boundary.
Pulls this shorter ball away on the leg side and comes back for the second.

Almost! Dangerous shot to play. Sliding in from over the wicket, on off, Das tries to cut and almost chops it back on. Could have even been bowled. So close. Lucky for him he managed to get a bottom edge on it.
Off the mark with a single. Pushes it to covers and gets to the other end.
Spinning away from around off, taps it down in front of point for nothing.
Outside off, Soumya brings out the reverse sweep only to miss. Bit of an unnecessary shot to play when he hasn't even opened his account. Should ideally get his eye in first.
Comes from around the wicket and bowls a flatter delivery, Sarkar gets an inside edge onto his pads as he tries working it across the line.
Spinning in on middle stump, Das works it down towards short fine leg for a single.
Mohammad Nabi comes on to bowl.
Steps out of his crease and once again offers a defensive shot. Ends of a superb over from Mujeeb.
Some flight offered on this occasion, Sarkar blocks it on the off side.
Soumya Sarkar walks in at no.3.

OUT! GONE! Mujeeb, the young maestro, continues to weave his magic as he dismisses the prolific Tamim Iqbal. Full around off from around the wicket, Tamim comes down the track and drives this towards the covers. Unfortunately for him, he can't keep it down and it's straight into the hands of Rasooli (sub) there. Early breakthrough for the home side.
Stays back and keeps it out off the back foot.
FOUR! Safest place to hit if you want to take the aerial route. Tamim uses his feet to come down the track, gets close to the pitch and lofts it over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Looped up by Mujeeb in line of the stumps, it's swept through to deep square leg for a run.
Shaping away on a fullish length, Tamim pushes it off the front foot to the cover fielder.

Good effort from Rashid Khan in the deep. Shortish on the stumps, Das pulls it through backward square leg. The leggie out in the deep covers a lot of ground to his right and keeps it from the boundary line. Keeps the batsmen down to two.

FOUR! Makes superb connection this time and sends it all the way. On the shorter side of the length, but it's a fraction too straight in line. Liton Das camps back and muscles the pull across the mid-wicket fence for a boundary.
Das gives the charge and seeing this, Alam shortens his length. Angles it in and cramps the batsman for room, thereby forcing him to miss his shot and taking a blow in the mid section.

Just over the fielder! Short of a length just outside off, it zips off the deck and hurries Liton Das who top edges his pull shot. Just about manages to clear Mohammad Nabi at mid on who can't get to it. Two runs taken.
Shaping back in on middle and leg, on a length, Das moves inside the line and pushes it in front of mid on.
Aftab Alam to bowl from the other end.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

OOH! In the air.. and safe. Just over the mid-wicket fielder. The batsman tries to flick the flighted delivery away with a wristy shot but gets a top edge. The ball lobs in the air for a while but just clears the fielder. In the end, they pick up a single.
No run. The Umpire declines the appeal. The flighted delivery from Mujeeb hits Das on his pad, who was out of his crease to meet the ball.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Stays in his crease to play the floated delivery outside and gets it to the short square leg region for a single.
Wide! The ball is down the leg side but the batsman still goes after it and misses. The Umpire signals a wide.
Mujeeb starts the proceedings with a flighted delivery on the middle stumps and Das punches it to mid off for a single.

We are back for the chase. It will be Tamim Iqbal and Liton Das to get things underway for the visiting side with the bat. Mujeeb Ur Rahman will take the ball first up for the Afghans. Drama already. Shahzad has a few words to say to the batters, due to which, the umpire had to intervene. We are now set to go. Let's roll...
